summary: Charm transport and hadronization, pion femtoscopy and Coulomb corrections, directed flow in baryon-rich matter, noncritical net-proton cumulants, neural cluster-state calculations, and conditional posterior inference.

papers.title: Open Heavy Flavor in Nuclear Collisions: From Lattice QCD to Observables
papers.short_authors: Yu Fu, Steffen A. Bass, Tharun Krishna, Ralf Rapp, Weiyao Ke
papers.summary: A lattice-constrained T-matrix transport framework combines Langevin diffusion, radiation, two hadronization schemes and hadronic rescattering. It compares D mesons and charm baryons with RHIC and LHC suppression, flow and yield-ratio data.
papers.abstract: A lattice-constrained T-matrix transport framework combines Langevin diffusion, radiation, two hadronization schemes and hadronic rescattering. It compares D mesons and charm baryons with RHIC and LHC suppression, flow and yield-ratio data.
papers.assessment: Broad comparisons and component studies make this a particularly useful framework paper. Lattice constraints do not eliminate phenomenological assumptions in radiation, hadronization and late rescattering; agreement is not a unique extraction of diffusion.

papers.title: Third-body-corrected Two-Pion Femtoscopic Correlations in Au+Au Collisions at High Baryon Density
papers.summary: STAR pion correlations from 3.0 to 7.7 GeV show charge-dependent HBT radii becoming consistent after a third-body Coulomb correction. The authors report a residual relative difference below 5% at 95% confidence.
papers.abstract: STAR pion correlations from 3.0 to 7.7 GeV show charge-dependent HBT radii becoming consistent after a third-body Coulomb correction. The authors report a residual relative difference below 5% at 95% confidence.
papers.assessment: A valuable control of a potential background to isospin-sensitive femtoscopy. This is a short proceedings contribution; the bound depends on the effective Coulomb correction and its uncertainties, including extrapolated potentials.

papers.title: Observation of Strong Directed Flow for phi Mesons in the High Baryon Density Region at RHIC
papers.summary: STAR fixed-target Au+Au results show phi-meson directed flow comparable in magnitude to proton and Lambda flow and larger than K-short flow at high baryon density. UrQMD comparisons are consistent with baryon-resonance production and baryonic mean-field effects.
papers.abstract: STAR fixed-target Au+Au results show phi-meson directed flow comparable in magnitude to proton and Lambda flow and larger than K-short flow at high baryon density. UrQMD comparisons are consistent with baryon-resonance production and baryonic mean-field effects.
papers.assessment: A useful species-dependent constraint on strange-hadron dynamics. The proposed production mechanism is model-supported, not uniquely established by the comparison.

papers.title: Study on net-proton number fluctuations in Au+Au collisions at 7.7-27 GeV with the SMASH model
papers.short_authors: Fengxi Yan, Ting Liu, Rongrong Ma, Yunshuang Qin, Shule Wu, Shenghui Zhang, Fan Si
papers.summary: SMASH calculations provide a noncritical baseline for cumulant ratios with STAR-like acceptance and centrality treatment. At 19.6 GeV the central C4/C2 data-model pull is about -2.7, compared with about -4.0 against UrQMD under the authors' uncertainty prescription.
papers.abstract: SMASH calculations provide a noncritical baseline for cumulant ratios with STAR-like acceptance and centrality treatment. At 19.6 GeV the central C4/C2 data-model pull is about -2.7, compared with about -4.0 against UrQMD under the authors' uncertainty prescription.
papers.assessment: An informative test of reference-model dependence, not a critical-point discovery. SMASH also systematically overshoots peripheral measurements; the diagnostic pull assumes independent uncertainty components.

papers.title: Nuclear Mott transition with neural quantum states
papers.short_authors: Zi-Xiao Zhang, Xiao-Lu Qian, Wan-Bing He, Gerd Röpke, Kai-Jia Sun, Yu-Gang Ma
papers.summary: A self-attention neural quantum state solves an in-medium few-body problem and is benchmarked against exact diagonalization for the deuteron. The authors predict much weaker alpha suppression and large abundance changes compared with approximate calculations.
papers.abstract: A self-attention neural quantum state solves an in-medium few-body problem and is benchmarked against exact diagonalization for the deuteron. The authors predict much weaker alpha suppression and large abundance changes compared with approximate calculations.
papers.assessment: A substantive use of ML on a difficult microscopic problem relevant to heavy-ion cluster yields. The exact benchmark is for the two-body system, not independent validation of the four-body result; the claimed explanation of collision data remains model-dependent.

papers.title: Amortized conditional inference under changing parameter information in small-angle X-ray scattering
papers.short_authors: Maria Bånkestad, Sandra Barman, Erik Kaunisto, Eskil Andreasson, Smita Chakraborty, Shun Yu, Jerk Rönnols, Sepideh Pashami
papers.summary: Masked flow matching estimates conditional posteriors under changing parameter information without retraining. The study checks analytic posteriors, compares architectures in a simulated scattering benchmark and analyzes experimental SAXS ambiguities.
papers.abstract: Masked flow matching estimates conditional posteriors under changing parameter information without retraining. The study checks analytic posteriors, compares architectures in a simulated scattering benchmark and analyzes experimental SAXS ambiguities.
papers.assessment: Potential transfer: recondition heavy-ion simulation-based inference on changing nuisance constraints. This is a concrete methodological analogy, not a demonstrated HEP application; calibration and simulator mismatch would need dedicated validation.
